newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco optimistic no Budel impact.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco optimistic no Budel impact.

text.p: Pasminco Ltd said on Sunday it was optimistic that delayed development of the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in Australia would not affect the continued operation of its Budel smelter in the Netherlands.

David Stewart, managing director of the Melbourne-based miner, said in a television interview that the company hoped to avoid any shutdown of Budel because it did not receive the clean, low iron concentrates from Century which the smelter required to end jarosite waste dumping.

Pasminco, the world's largest zinc producer, last month agreed to buy the mine in northwestern Queensland from mining house RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd for A$345 million, subject to the mine receiving valid leases.

Attempts to reach a negotiated settlement between RTZ-CRA unit Century Zinc and aboriginal groups which claim ownership of the land collapsed last Thursday, forcing the talks into the next phase of an arbitrated settlement under the Australian government's native title legislation process. The arbitration phase could take up to six months.
Pasminco managing director David Stewart, interviewed on the Nine Network's Business Sunday programme, said he was disappointed that negotiations had failed.
"But we had always factored into our thinking that the process would go into the next phase of the native title negotiation, which is the arbitration phase," Stewart said.
"And we are quite confident that as a result of that ... the mine will get the go-ahead eventually."
At the moment, Pasminco was a keen observer of the Century talks rather than a party to the talks, he said.
Pasminco said last Friday that the timetable to begin development of the mine and to coordinate this with the supply of zinc concentrate to its Budel smelter had now tightened considerably.

Stewart said the possibility of moving the Century talks into arbitration had been factored into talks last year with the Dutch government which led to Pasminco receiving a two-year extension to July 1, 2000, when Budel's licence for jarosite storage expired.
Asked if Budel might close because the end-1997 Century development timetable might not be met, he said; "I think the end of the year is still manageable."
